known.title: Decision 5 tells the agent to write a private number as `GH-123` and says that GitHub does not link it, but GitHub links `GH-123` to issue 123 of the same repository.
known.summary: Decision 5 makes the new Gotchas row say: write a number from a private project as `GH-123`, "which GitHub does not link". The GitHub documentation (https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/writing-on-github/working-with-advanced-formatting/autolinked-references-and-urls, section "Issues and pull requests") lists "`GH-` and issue or pull request number" (raw reference `GH-26`) as a reference type that GitHub converts to a link to issue 26 of the same repository. Its section "Avoiding backlinks to linked references" says: "By default, references generate a backlink." The skill files every report in DocksDocks/docks (`plugins/docks/skills/productivity/report-skill-issue/SKILL.md:111` at repo_ref). So `GH-123` in a report links to DocksDocks/docks#123, an unrelated issue, and adds a backlink on that issue. This is the same failure that the plan's own fact (line 18) gives for `#123`. Effect: the shipped Gotchas row teaches a form that causes the defect that it must stop. Expected: write the number as plain text with no `#` and no `GH-` prefix (for example "issue 123 in a private repository", as decision 2 says).

known.title: Decision 2 counts the project as public when no lookup prints `PRIVATE`, so a project in an `INTERNAL` repository counts as public and its names go into the public issue.
known.locator: Research, Decisions, decision 2, sentence "The project counts as public only when ..." (line 27)
known.summary: Decision 2 counts the user's project as public when it has at least one remote, every remote is on `github.com`, and no `gh repo view github.com/<owner>/<repo> --json visibility --jq .visibility` lookup prints `PRIVATE`. The gh field `visibility` (https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_repo_view, JSON Fields) is the GraphQL field `Repository.visibility` of type `RepositoryVisibility`. That enum has three values (https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/repos, "RepositoryVisibility - enum"): `INTERNAL` ("The repository is visible only to users in the same enterprise."), `PRIVATE`, and `PUBLIC`. The GitHub Enterprise Cloud documentation (https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/repositories/creating-and-managing-repositories/about-repositories) says: "Internal repositories are not visible to people outside of the enterprise", and internal is the default for new repositories in an organization that an enterprise account owns. So for a project with an internal remote, the lookup succeeds and prints `INTERNAL`. That is not `PRIVATE`, and the failed-lookup clause does not apply, so the project counts as public. The draft then keeps the project's owner, repository name, issue and pull request titles, branch names, and `#`-numbers, and the skill files the draft in the public DocksDocks/docks repository (`plugins/docks/skills/productivity/report-skill-issue/SKILL.md:15-16` and `:20` at repo_ref: anyone can read its issues; leave out names of private repositories and organizations and titles of private issues). The Goal (line 5) says that a project that is not public contributes none of these names. Expected: count the project as public only when every lookup prints `PUBLIC`, as the rule for other repositories in the same decision does.

known.title: Decision 2 adds a sentence to the Report section of this skill only, but that section must stay byte-identical in all 31 shipped skills, and the plan allows no edit outside this skill.
known.locator: Research, Decisions, decision 2, sentence "The second constraint and the Report section at the end of the skill each add one sentence" (line 27); Steps, row 2 visibility_check, Files cell (line 42); Do not touch (lines 56-59)
known.summary: Decision 2 makes the Report section at the end of `plugins/docks/skills/productivity/report-skill-issue/SKILL.md` add the sentence "decide visibility with that lookup, not from memory", and the Do not touch list no longer protects that section. At repo_ref, `plugins/docks/skills/AGENTS.md:105-107` owns the rule: every shipped skill of the docks and plan-lifecycle plugins ends with one byte-identical `## Report a problem with this skill` section, "a change to the section changes every copy in the same commit", and the verify command must print one line. `plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/AGENTS.md:92-96` repeats that the section is byte-identical across both plugins. At repo_ref, 31 shipped `SKILL.md` files hold the section, all with one hash; this skill's copy is `plugins/docks/skills/productivity/report-skill-issue/SKILL.md:254-256`. The plan changes only that copy: step 2 lists only this file (line 42), and Do not touch keeps "Files outside `plugins/docks/skills/productivity/report-skill-issue/` before the release step" (line 59). So the other 30 copies, the second owners of the same text, stay unchanged, and the verify command prints two lines. The sentence also does not fit the other copies, because "that lookup" is the stage 4 lookup of this skill only. a1 does not catch the break: no script at repo_ref checks the section (`git grep 'Report a problem'` finds no `.mjs` or `.js` file). Expected: keep the Report section unchanged and put the sentence in the second constraint only, or change all 31 copies in one commit and list that change in Files and Acceptance.

known.title: Acceptance a3 tests a title whose only special character is an apostrophe, which the old double-quoted stage 6 command and link scripts already pass unchanged.
known.summary: a3 runs the fake-gh experiment with the title `docks:report-skill-issue: don't drop the title` and expects it to arrive unchanged. At repo_ref, stage 6 passes the title inline in double quotes (`gh issue create --repo DocksDocks/docks --title "<approved title>" --body-file "$body"`, `plugins/docks/skills/productivity/report-skill-issue/SKILL.md:111`), and both link scripts take `"<approved title>"` as a double-quoted argument (`:129` and `:131`). The Bash manual (https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/html_node/Double-Quotes.html) says: "Enclosing characters in double quotes preserves the literal value of all characters within the quotes, with the exception of '$', '`', '\', and, when history expansion is enabled, '!'." The a3 title has none of these characters, so the unchanged command and the unchanged scripts pass it unchanged (checked with Bash 5.3.9 and a fake `gh` that prints its arguments; the Node and Python link scripts also encode it so that decoding gives it back unchanged). An apostrophe breaks only a single-quoted title, which decision 1 rejects; the failure in the plan's fact (line 22) comes from a word in backticks. Effect: a3 passes without decision 1 and does not show that the change keeps the title. Expected: a3 uses a title with a word in backticks and `$` (as step 1's Done when says), which the old command changes and the new command keeps.
